title: Fearchar's petition for the coal
summary: Fearchar mac Ruairidh comes to Taigh na Fèithe and asks that each hull found fit to sail be allowed to carry one sealed measure of the coal, no more than a single household's season under Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig. The custodians send him down the hill with a promise only to put the matter to the board.

title: The custodians' debate at the winter burning
summary: After six winters of argument Taigh na Fèithe's board finally votes on Fearchar's petition. Cailean and others hold that the coal has never crossed water and should not; Fearchar answers that Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig measures a hearth wherever a hearth chooses to stand. Leabhar a' Chùraim is opened and the question is put to writing.

title: The fair copy of the ruling, Donnchadh's first entry
summary: Donnchadh mac Thormoid, the boy-clerk, is set at fifteen to render the ruling clean for Leabhar a' Chùraim, after it has lain four years in rough marks: one sealed measure a ship, a single household's season, Taigh na Fèithe's own mark. He copies it exactly as given, though he notices it carries no blessing, as other entries do.

title: Death of Eòghann mac Mhuirich
summary: The master of Taigh na Fèithe, who wrote the first count of the departing households in LE 3, dies at Taigh na Fèithe grown very old, soon after seeing the ruling of the coal for the departing set down and its first measures sealed.

title: The sealed measures made
summary: The first measures of coal are weighed and sealed at Taigh na Fèithe, each against the words "for each hull that shall be ready", with no count kept against any known number of hulls. Fearchar mac Ruairidh stands by in silence to see the first one made.

title: The queen lends masons for the quay
summary: Beathag nic Dhòmhnaill sends a gang of masons from the capital, under Ailean mac Nèill, down to Seann Skell to lengthen the west quay with dressed stone "for the harbour's trade", the crown's word for it and no other named.

title: The queen at Seann Skell to see the stones laid
summary: Beathag rides the twenty-four miles to Seann Skell and stands on the new-laid stone of the west quay in the evening light, the only time she is known to have come to see the fleet's building with her own eyes. Her sister Mòrag joins her there, and the two speak of small things, not of the roll.

title: Death of Uilleam mac Iain, the queen's consort
summary: Uilleam mac Iain, husband to Queen Beathag and father of her son, dies after a summer's illness. The queen keeps the funeral small, a single day at Cathair dhearg with the household and a few custodian heads, and no great muster of the shires.

title: Donnchadh mac Thormoid given to Taigh na Fèithe
summary: Tormod, a turf-cutter of the moor above Muileann dhearg, walks his son Donnchadh, nine years old, up the coal-road to Taigh na Fèithe and leaves him there sworn to the vein's service for seven years, and does not look back.

title: The iron cramp of the last stone
summary: Ailean mac Nèill's gang sets the last stone of the lengthened quay at the seaward end, where the new masonry meets the old timber staging, and Ailean drives home the iron cramp that binds them with three blows and no more.
